title: Plants need water and light
keyIdea: A plant needs water and light to stay healthy, and it needs to be warm enough. When the soil is dry, the plant droops, so you give it water. Wet soil does not need more: too much water can rot the roots. A plant kept in the dark grows tall, thin and pale, so tall is not the same as healthy. Plants grow toward the light, which is why a plant on a windowsill leans to the window.

kid: A plant drinks water from the soil. Touch the soil. Is it dry? Give it water. Is it wet? Wait.
No water? The plant droops. Its leaves hang down. Give it water and it stands up again.
A plant needs light too. Put a plant in a dark cupboard. It grows tall and thin. Its leaves go pale. It is not well.
A plant leans to the light. Put it by a window. It bends to the window.
adult: This is early plant biology. In the EYFS, Development Matters asks three and four year olds to plant seeds and care for growing plants, and England's Year 2 science asks children to find out and describe how plants need water, light and a suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy. US NGSS K-LS1-1 asks children to describe what plants need to live, using what they see.

Roots take up water from the soil; without it the plant wilts because its cells lose the water that keeps them firm. Leaves use light to make the plant's food (photosynthesis), so a plant grown in the dark stretches into tall, thin, pale shoots, which botanists call etiolation. A plant bends toward light from one side, called phototropism.

Common mistakes: thinking more water is always better (waterlogged soil starves roots of air and they can rot), thinking the tallest plant is the healthiest, thinking a plant in the dark will not grow at all, and thinking plants eat food from the soil the way we eat. A common adult slip is watering on a fixed schedule instead of checking whether the soil is dry first.

In the lab your child waters a pot plant over five days, but only when the soil is dry. Next, they read the clue on a sad plant and give it water or light. They grow two seedlings, one in a dark cupboard, and compare them. They move a lamp and watch the plant lean to it. Last, they sort what a plant needs.

familyTip: Grow cress or a bean on two saucers: one on the windowsill and one in a cupboard. Check them together each day and let your child decide when to water by touching the soil. After a week, compare: which one is green and strong?

visual.caption: What does this plant need? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Tall, thin and pale in the dark
Leaves hang down on a hot day
Green leaves on a sunny windowsill

lab.caption: Flagship lab: water only when the soil is dry, fix droopy and pale plants, grow a seedling in a cupboard, move a lamp and sort what plants need.

practice.prompt: A plant on the windowsill droops. Its soil is dry. What does it need?
practice.hint: Look at the soil. What is missing?
practice.explain: Dry soil means the roots have no water to drink. Water it and the leaves stand up again.

practice.prompt: Kit has {n} plants. She puts 1 in a dark cupboard and the rest on the windowsill. How many plants have light?
practice.hint: Take away the one in the cupboard.
practice.explain: {n} plants with 1 in the dark leaves {=n-1} plants in the light.

practice.prompt: The soil is still wet. Do you water the plant again?
choices: No, wait until it is dry
Yes, fill the pot to the top
practice.hint: Can roots get too much water?
practice.explain: Too much water can rot the roots. Wait until the soil feels dry, then water.

practice.prompt: Your bean plant is {a} blocks tall. With water and light it grows {b} blocks more. How tall is it now?
practice.hint: Start at {a} and count on {b} more.
practice.explain: {a} blocks and {b} more blocks make {=a+b} blocks tall. Water and light helped it grow.

pool.prompt: A plant grew in a dark cupboard. What does it look like?
pool.hint: What does a plant need light for?
pool.explain: In the dark, a plant stretches up looking for light. It grows thin, and its leaves go pale.

pool.prompt: Two plants: a tall pale one from the cupboard and a short green one from the window. Which is healthy?
pool.hint: Is taller always better? Think about what the cupboard plant was missing.
pool.explain: The green one had light and is strong. The tall pale one is thin and floppy because it had no light.

pool.prompt: A plant is next to a window. Which way does it lean?
pool.hint: Where does the light come from?
pool.explain: Plants grow toward the light, so it bends to the window.

pool.prompt: What does a plant need to stay healthy?
pool.hint: Think of the droopy plant and the pale plant.
pool.explain: A plant needs water and light, and to be warm enough. Water alone is not enough.

pool.prompt: {n} plants are on the windowsill. {k} have dry soil. How many need water?
pool.hint: Which plants need water: the dry ones or the wet ones?
pool.explain: Only the plants with dry soil need water, so {k} need water. The others can wait.

pool.prompt: How can you tell if a plant needs water?
choices: Touch the soil: is it dry?
pool.hint: Where does the plant get its water from?
pool.explain: The roots drink from the soil. Dry soil means it is time to water.

pool.prompt: You water a plant on day 1. Its soil is dry again after {d} days. On which day do you water it next?
pool.hint: Start at day 1 and count on {d} days.
pool.explain: Day 1 and {d} more days is day {=1+d}. The soil is dry then, so that is when to water.

pool.prompt: A pale plant has wet soil and sits in a dark corner. What does it need?
pool.hint: The soil is wet already. What else is missing?
pool.explain: The soil is wet, so water is not the problem. Pale leaves in the dark mean it needs light.
